**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare decreases to the new source revision**

When a graph refresh legitimately removes or renames a symbol, the prescribed `--repo-ref <base>` makes the script read the pre-change source via `git show <base>:<path>`, where the removed definition still exists. It therefore reports the correct lower count as `REGRESSION` rather than explained, forcing a manual exception for every legitimate deletion and undermining the automatic gate. Pass the revision that produced the new graph (normally `HEAD`) instead of the previous graph's base.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

If `--repo-ref` is absent from a shallow checkout or is mistyped, `git show` fails for every path, but this branch returns `None` and the caller labels each lost file `gone` and `explained`. A graph that drops every symbol then exits successfully, bypassing the coverage gate. Validate the revision separately and treat a failed `git show` as a missing file only after confirming that the revision itself resolves.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize uv-script Python executables**

Extensionless Python executables launched through `uv run --script` are not recognized as Python because only a `.py` suffix or `python` in the first line is checked. This repository's `home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_permgate` has the `uv` shebang and 16 UA function/class nodes, so a legitimate source deletion in that file is always reported as `REGRESSION` rather than explained, forcing a manual exception for valid graph refreshes. Detect Python script metadata (such as `requires-python`) or otherwise recognize this supported executable form.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Put the coverage helper on Codex's PATH**

Codex workers are required to run this bare command, but the managed `[shell_environment_policy]` renders `PATH` from `home/dot_agents/agent-config.yaml:122` without `~/.local/bin/common`; the helper is installed only as `~/.local/bin/common/ua-symbol-coverage`. Consequently, a managed Codex worker cannot execute the mandatory graph-acceptance check (`command not found`) even after `chezmoi apply`. Include the common-bin directory in the rendered PATH or invoke the helper by its absolute path.

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare renamed paths before exempting disappearances**

When a source file is renamed and the new graph omits its symbols, the old path is automatically marked `explained` because it is absent at the new ref, while the renamed path has `old == 0` and is therefore `ok`; the gate exits 0 despite losing the entire renamed file's coverage. Fresh evidence: renaming `pkg/a.py` (two definitions) to `pkg/b.py` and giving the new graph only a `pkg/b.py` file node produces `a.py: explained`, `b.py: ok`, and `regressions: 0`. Match renames/moves (or otherwise compare source-backed new paths) before treating an absent old path as an explained loss.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:6b53337

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve coverage across low-similarity moves**

When a source file is moved and substantially rewritten, Git's default `-M` threshold emits a delete/add pair rather than a rename. The old path is then automatically marked `explained` as deleted while the new path has `old == 0`, so omitted symbols in the new file are never compared. Fresh evidence: moving `a.py` to `b.py`, retaining its two definitions while adding 80 rewritten lines, and emitting only a `b.py` file node makes this command return 0 with `a.py: explained` and `b.py: ok`. Match such moves before exempting disappeared paths, or fail closed when a source-backed added path has no historical coverage.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:c878b0d

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize visibility-prefixed Ruby definitions**

For Ruby files using valid `private def` (or `protected def`) syntax, this pattern omits the private method while still counting the enclosing class and public methods. Consequently, a graph changing from one class plus two methods to one class plus one method yields `defs == 2`, satisfies `after >= min(before, defs)`, and exits successfully even though the private definition remains in source and its node was lost. Include visibility-prefixed method declarations in the source count so this gate does not approve that incomplete graph.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:c878b0d

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject partially covered source-backed additions**

When a graph refresh adds a source file (including a low-similarity move) with multiple definitions but emits only some of its symbols, `after` is nonzero and this condition is skipped, so the command exits 0. Fresh evidence: a new `b.py` containing two `def` lines with one function node produces `| b.py | 0 | 1 | 2 | ok |` and `regressions: 0`. This allows the new acceptance rule to approve an incomplete graph; compare source-backed new paths against their definition count even when they retain some nodes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: not-applicable:measured on the accepted graph: 138 of 185 grammar files already have fewer function/class nodes than def-like lines (UA emits no node for most methods and nested functions), so new < defs cannot gate; documented ceiling in the helper docstring (56f308c); only the zero-symbol case is flagged

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize valid punctuation in shell function names**

Bash accepts names such as `function foo? { :; }`, but this pattern excludes `?` (and other valid shell word characters). If a revision changes an unrelated line in such a file and the refreshed graph loses that node, the old/new blobs differ, the counter sees only the remaining ordinary function, and the loss is labeled `explained`; a two-function `x.sh` with `foo?` and `bar` reproduced as `old=2, new=1, defs=1`, exiting 0. Broaden the shell-definition matcher or use a shell-aware parser so these losses remain regressions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:afb2c9d

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Detect definitions added during a rename**

When a detected rename also adds definitions, `judged` excludes the successor from the new-file completeness check. Fresh evidence: renaming `a.py` to `b.py`, adding a second `def`, and retaining only the original function node exits 0 (`a.py` is `ok` and `b.py` is skipped), so an accepted refresh can omit the newly added symbol. Apply the `after < defs` check to renamed successors as well while retaining the predecessor-count comparison.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: not-applicable:same class as the partially-covered finding — a successor that keeps at least the old count but gains definitions is partial under-extraction, which the def-line count cannot gate (138 of 185 measurement); the rename row still fails closed when the successor drops below the old count; documented ceiling (56f308c docstring)

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail closed for low-similarity moves in other languages**

For a low-similarity move in a source type without a def grammar, `def_pattern` returns `None`, so this type guard skips the only check on the added path while the old path is treated as an explained deletion. Fresh evidence: moving a two-function `a.js` to a heavily rewritten `b.js` and emitting only a `b.js` file node returns 0 with `a.js` explained and `b.js` `ok`, losing all symbols. Add coverage for graph-supported source languages or fail closed for unrecognized source-backed additions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:c878b0d

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare the source tree against graph paths**

When a newly added supported source file is omitted entirely from the refreshed graph (so it has neither a file node nor a symbol node), it is absent from `set(old) | set(new)` and `def_lines` is never called for it. For example, adding a `b.py` with two functions while leaving the new graph unchanged produces `regressions: 0`; this lets the completeness gate approve precisely the extractor failure the new-file check is intended to catch. Enumerate relevant source paths at `--repo-ref` (subject to the graph's ignore rules) or otherwise fail when source-backed files are absent from the new graph.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
items.disposition: fixed:72746d4

items.author: chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]
items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid counting docstring text as Python definitions**

For a newly added Python file that correctly has no function/class nodes but contains a multiline string whose line starts with `def`, this regex reports a definition and the zero-symbol check rejects the graph. A file containing only `DOC = """\ndef not_a_real_function():\n"""` reproduces this as `REGRESSION | new file, no symbols`; use Python parsing or otherwise exclude string literals before applying this gate.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

The following taps are not trusted:
  aws/tap
  azure/bicep
  hashicorp/tap

Homebrew is currently ignoring formulae, casks and commands from these taps because tap trust is required.

Prefer trusting only the specific formulae, casks or commands you need.
Trust installed formulae from these taps with:
  brew trust --formula azure/bicep/bicep
  brew trust --formula hashicorp/tap/packer
Trust other specific casks and commands with:
  brew trust --cask <user>/<tap>/<cask>
  brew trust --command <user>/<tap>/<command>
Whole-tap trust is broader and includes all current and future formulae,
casks and commands from the listed taps. Trust whole taps with:
  brew trust aws/tap azure/bicep hashicorp/tap
Untap them with:
  brew untap aws/tap azure/bicep hashicorp/tap
To disable trust checks:
  export HOMEBREW_NO_REQUIRE_TAP_TRUST=1
This is not recommended and will be removed in a later release.
For more information, see:
  https://docs.brew.sh/Tap-Trust
